subject: maths
title: Year 6 Timetables and Itineraries
seo_title: Year 6 Timetables and Itineraries Worksheets: Reading Timetables, Journey Times and Planning (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Interpret and use timetables and itineraries to plan activities and determine the duration of events and journeys
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on timetables and itineraries for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6M03): read bus, train and ferry timetables in 24-hour time, work out journey times across hours and midnight, choose the right service to arrive on time and plan a school camp or day trip. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Find the row for the stop and the column for the service. The time is where they meet.
key_sub: To find how long a journey takes, count on to the next o’clock in jumps: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100. To arrive on time, work backwards from the time you must be there and pick the latest service that gets you there.
body_html:
Reading a timetable

A timetable lists the stops down the side. Each column is one bus, train or ferry. To read it, find the row for the stop and the column for the service. The time is where they meet. A dash (—) means the service does not stop there. Most timetables use 24-hour time.

Read across and down

A train leaves Richmond at 07:55. What time does it get to Cheltenham?

Find 07:55 in the Richmond row. Go down that column (not across) to the Cheltenham row.

Answer: 08:21

How long is the journey? Count on in jumps

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers. Jump to the next o’clock, then on in whole hours, then to the end time. If the journey goes past midnight, count on through 00:00.

Journey time

A train leaves Central at 09:18 and gets to Penrith at 10:11. How long is the trip?

09:18 to 10:00 is 42 minutes. 10:00 to 10:11 is 11 minutes. 42 + 11 = 53.

Answer: 53 minutes

Plan to arrive on time: work backwards

Start from the time you must be there. Count back any walking or waiting, then choose the latest service that arrives at or before that time.

Which train?

The footy starts at 19:40. The train takes 25 minutes and the walk takes 10 minutes. Trains leave at 18:52, 19:07 and 19:22. Which is the latest train?

19:40 − 10 minutes = 19:30. 19:30 − 25 minutes = 19:05. The latest train not after 19:05 is 18:52.

Answer: 18:52

Itineraries

An itinerary is a plan for a day or a trip. Each activity usually ends when the next one starts, so subtract start times to find how long each part lasts. When a trip crosses time zones, use the local time. In winter, Perth is 2 hours behind Sydney.

Camp itinerary

Canoeing starts at 13:00 and afternoon tea starts at 14:45. How long is canoeing?

13:00 to 14:00 is 1 hour. 14:00 to 14:45 is 45 minutes.

Answer: 1 hour 45 minutes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the time next to the right one (the wrong row or the wrong column)Put a finger on the row and another on the column, and read where they meet
09:18 to 10:11 worked out as 1011 − 918 = 93 minutesAn hour has 60 minutes. Count on: 42 + 11 = 53 minutes
4:20 pm read as 14:20Add 12 to a pm hour: 4 + 12 = 16, so 16:20
Catching the train that arrives just after the start timeChoose the latest service that arrives at or before the time you need
Adding the walking time when you should count backWork backwards from the time you must be there
22:35 to 01:10 worked out as 22:35 − 01:10Count on through midnight: 25 minutes + 2 hours + 10 minutes

faq.q: What do Year 6 students learn about timetables and itineraries?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum v9.0 (AC9M6M03), Year 6 students Interpret and use timetables and itineraries to plan activities and work out how long events and journeys take, using 24-hour time.

faq.q: How do you read a bus or train timetable?
faq.a: Find the row for your stop and the column for your service; the time is where they meet. To plan a trip, look along the row where you want to arrive and choose the latest service that gets there in time.

faq.q: How do you work out how long a journey takes when it goes past midnight?
faq.a: Count on in jumps: from the start time to midnight (00:00), then on to the end time. For example, 22:35 to 01:10 is 25 minutes + 2 hours + 10 minutes = 2 hours 35 minutes.

faq.q: How many hours is Perth behind Sydney?
faq.a: Perth is 2 hours behind Sydney from April to early October. When New South Wales uses daylight saving (early October to early April) the difference is 3 hours, because Western Australia does not use daylight saving.

sets.title: Read bus, train and ferry timetables

items.q: Leo catches the train that leaves Flinders Street at 07:24. What time does he get to Cheltenham?
items.e: Find 07:24 in the Flinders Street row. Go down that column to the Cheltenham row: 07:54. (Stay in the same column: the times next to it belong to other trains.)

items.q: What time does the first train on the timetable leave Caulfield?
items.e: Each column is one train, in time order from left to right. Count 1 column from the left, then go down to the Caulfield row: 07:27.

items.q: A train gets to Caulfield at 08:06. What time did it leave Flinders Street?
items.e: Find 08:06 in the Caulfield row. Go up that column to the Flinders Street row: 07:51.

items.q: The train that leaves Flinders Street at 07:39 is an express. Which station does it not stop at?
items.e: A dash (—) means the train does not stop there. In the 07:39 column the dash is in the Cheltenham row. This train is an express, so it gets to Frankston sooner (08:31).

items.q: The train that leaves Flinders Street at 07:12 stops somewhere at 07:42. Where is it?
items.e: Find the train that leaves Flinders Street at 07:12. Go down that column until you reach 07:42. It is in the Cheltenham row.

items.q: Amelia catches the bus that leaves City (Queen Street) at 15:58. What time does she get to Carindale?
items.e: Find 15:58 in the City (Queen Street) row. Go down that column to the Carindale row: 16:31. (Stay in the same column: the times next to it belong to other buses.)

items.q: What time does the fourth bus on the timetable leave South Bank?
items.e: Each column is one bus, in time order from left to right. Count 4 columns from the left, then go down to the South Bank row: 16:31.

items.q: A bus gets to Coorparoo at 15:54. What time did it leave South Bank?
items.e: Find 15:54 in the Coorparoo row. Go up that column to the South Bank row: 15:41.

items.q: The bus that leaves City (Queen Street) at 15:58 stops somewhere at 16:09. Where is it?
items.e: Find the bus that leaves City (Queen Street) at 15:58. Go down that column until you reach 16:09. It is in the Woolloongabba row.

items.q: Kai catches the bus that leaves City (Queen Street) at 3:05 pm. What time does he get to Coorparoo, in 12-hour time?
items.e: 3:05 pm is 15:05 in 24-hour time. Go down that column to Coorparoo: 15:24. 15 is more than 12, so it is pm. 15 − 12 = 3, so it is 3:24 pm.

items.q: Matilda catches the ferry that leaves Circular Quay at 11:05. What time does she get to Sydney Olympic Park?
items.e: Find 11:05 in the Circular Quay row. Go down that column to the Sydney Olympic Park row: 11:58. (Stay in the same column: the times next to it belong to other ferries.)

items.q: What time does the third ferry on the timetable leave Cockatoo Island?
items.e: Each column is one ferry, in time order from left to right. Count 3 columns from the left, then go down to the Cockatoo Island row: 12:11.

items.q: Cooper catches the ferry that leaves Circular Quay at 11:05 am. What time does he get to Parramatta, in 12-hour time?
items.e: 11:05 am is 11:05 in 24-hour time. Go down that column to Parramatta: 12:24. 12 is the hour just after midday, so it is pm: 12:24 pm.

items.q: A ferry gets to Parramatta at 13:54. What time did it leave Balmain?
items.e: Find 13:54 in the Parramatta row. Go up that column to the Balmain row: 12:47.

items.q: The ferry that leaves Circular Quay at 12:35 stops somewhere at 12:47. Where is it?
items.e: Find the ferry that leaves Circular Quay at 12:35. Go down that column until you reach 12:47. It is in the Balmain row.

items.q: Mia catches the train that leaves Subiaco at 23:21. What time does she get to Fremantle?
items.e: Find 23:21 in the Subiaco row. Go down that column to the Fremantle row: 23:43. (Stay in the same column: the times next to it belong to other trains.)

items.q: What time does the second train on the timetable leave Cottesloe?
items.e: Each column is one train, in time order from left to right. Count 2 columns from the left, then go down to the Cottesloe row: 23:04.

items.q: Ava catches the train that leaves Perth at 11:45 pm. What time does she get to Cottesloe, in 12-hour time?
items.e: 11:45 pm is 23:45 in 24-hour time. Go down that column to Cottesloe: 00:04. The hour 00 is just after midnight. In 12-hour time it is 12 am, so it is 12:04 am.

items.q: A train gets to Fremantle at 22:43. What time did it leave Perth?
items.e: Find 22:43 in the Fremantle row. Go up that column to the Perth row: 22:15.

items.q: Isla gets to Flinders Street at 07:30. Which train should she catch to get to Frankston as early as possible?
items.e: Look along the Frankston row: 08:11, 08:23, 08:31, 08:50. The train leaving at 07:39 arrives at 08:31, before the 07:51 train (08:50). If you are at Flinders Street at 07:30, the 07:24 has gone, so catch the 07:39: it gets there at 08:31.

sets.title: How long is the journey? Across hours and midnight

items.q: A tram leaves Glenelg at 13:38 and gets to the Adelaide city centre at 14:11. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 13:38 to 14:00 is 22 minutes, 14:00 to 14:11 is 11 minutes. 22 minutes + 11 minutes = 33 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: The Manly ferry leaves Circular Quay at 11:51 and gets to Manly at 12:21. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 11:51 to 12:00 is 9 minutes, 12:00 to 12:21 is 21 minutes. 9 minutes + 21 minutes = 30 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: A Canberra light rail tram leaves Gungahlin at 17:49 and gets to the city at 18:13. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 17:49 to 18:00 is 11 minutes, 18:00 to 18:13 is 13 minutes. 11 minutes + 13 minutes = 24 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: A train leaves Perth at 18:58 and gets to Mandurah at 19:49. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 18:58 to 19:00 is 2 minutes, 19:00 to 19:49 is 49 minutes. 2 minutes + 49 minutes = 51 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: A train leaves Central at 09:51 and gets to Wollongong at 11:18. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 09:51 to 10:00 is 9 minutes, 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour, 11:00 to 11:18 is 18 minutes. 1 hour + 9 minutes + 18 minutes = 1 hour 27 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: A coach leaves Sydney at 07:49 and gets to Canberra at 11:14. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 07:49 to 08:00 is 11 minutes, 08:00 to 11:00 is 3 hours, 11:00 to 11:14 is 14 minutes. 3 hours + 11 minutes + 14 minutes = 3 hours 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: A train leaves Brisbane at 09:49 and gets to Varsity Lakes on the Gold Coast at 11:07. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 09:49 to 10:00 is 11 minutes, 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour, 11:00 to 11:07 is 7 minutes. 1 hour + 11 minutes + 7 minutes = 1 hour 18 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: A train leaves Southern Cross station in Melbourne at 17:37 and gets to Ballarat at 19:01. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 17:37 to 18:00 is 23 minutes, 18:00 to 19:00 is 1 hour, 19:00 to 19:01 is 1 minute. 1 hour + 23 minutes + 1 minute = 1 hour 24 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long does the 09:18 train take from Central to Penrith?
items.e: In the 09:18 column, it leaves Central at 09:18 and gets to Penrith at 10:11. Count on: 09:18 to 10:00 is 42 minutes, 10:00 to 10:11 is 11 minutes. 42 minutes + 11 minutes = 53 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long does the 10:18 train take from Strathfield to Katoomba?
items.e: In the 10:18 column, it leaves Strathfield at 10:32 and gets to Katoomba at 12:19. Count on: 10:32 to 11:00 is 28 minutes, 11:00 to 12:00 is 1 hour, 12:00 to 12:19 is 19 minutes. 1 hour + 28 minutes + 19 minutes = 1 hour 47 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long does the 08:18 train take from Central to Mount Victoria?
items.e: In the 08:18 column, it leaves Central at 08:18 and gets to Mount Victoria at 10:41. Count on: 08:18 to 09:00 is 42 minutes, 09:00 to 10:00 is 1 hour, 10:00 to 10:41 is 41 minutes. 1 hour + 42 minutes + 41 minutes = 2 hours 23 minutes.

items.q: How long does the 11:18 train take from Penrith to Mount Victoria?
items.e: In the 11:18 column, it leaves Penrith at 12:11 and gets to Mount Victoria at 13:41. Count on: 12:11 to 13:00 is 49 minutes, 13:00 to 13:41 is 41 minutes. 49 minutes + 41 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes.

items.q: A Year 6 excursion bus leaves school at 9:45 am and gets back at 13:20. How long is the excursion?
items.e: Change 9:45 am to 09:45. Count on: 09:45 to 10:00 is 15 minutes, 10:00 to 13:00 is 3 hours, 13:00 to 13:20 is 20 minutes. 3 hours + 15 minutes + 20 minutes = 3 hours 35 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: A koala-spotting walk starts at 11:40 am and ends at 2:05 pm. How long is the walk?
items.e: It goes past midday, so count on from 11:40 am. Count on: 11:40 am to 12:00 pm is 20 minutes, 12:00 pm to 2:00 pm is 2 hours, 2:00 pm to 2:05 pm is 5 minutes. 2 hours + 20 minutes + 5 minutes = 2 hours 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Cooper’s family boards a dinner cruise at 18:50 and gets off at 9:15 pm. How long is the cruise?
items.e: 9:15 pm is 21:15. Count on: 18:50 to 19:00 is 10 minutes, 19:00 to 21:00 is 2 hours, 21:00 to 21:15 is 15 minutes. 2 hours + 10 minutes + 15 minutes = 2 hours 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Ruby catches a train at 08:12 that arrives at 08:47. She then catches a bus at 09:05 that arrives at 09:38. How long is her whole journey, from the start of the train to the end of the bus?
items.e: The whole journey is from 08:12 to 09:38, and that includes the wait between the train and the bus. Count on: 08:12 to 09:00 is 48 minutes, 09:00 to 09:38 is 38 minutes. 48 minutes + 38 minutes = 1 hour 26 minutes. (Adding only the two rides, 35 + 33 = 68 minutes, leaves out the wait.)

items.q: The last train leaves Flinders Street at 23:52 and gets to Frankston at 00:51. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 23:52 to 00:00 is 8 minutes, 00:00 to 00:51 is 51 minutes. 8 minutes + 51 minutes = 59 minutes. (Count on through midnight. Taking the smaller time from the bigger one gives the wrong answer.)

items.q: The last train of the night leaves Perth at 23:45 and gets to Fremantle at 00:13. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 23:45 to 00:00 is 15 minutes, 00:00 to 00:13 is 13 minutes. 15 minutes + 13 minutes = 28 minutes. (Count on through midnight. Taking the smaller time from the bigger one gives the wrong answer.)

items.q: On New Year’s Eve, Charlotte’s family leaves home at 22:35 to watch the midnight fireworks. They get home at 01:10. How long were they out?
items.e: Count on: 22:35 to 23:00 is 25 minutes, 23:00 to 01:00 is 2 hours, 01:00 to 01:10 is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 25 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 35 minutes. (Count on through midnight. Taking the smaller time from the bigger one gives the wrong answer.)

items.q: An overnight coach leaves Sydney at 19:15 and gets to Byron Bay at 08:35 the next morning. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 19:15 to 20:00 is 45 minutes, 20:00 to 08:00 is 12 hours, 08:00 to 08:35 is 35 minutes. 12 hours + 45 minutes + 35 minutes = 13 hours 20 minutes. (Count on through midnight. Taking the smaller time from the bigger one gives the wrong answer.)

sets.title: Which service? Plan to arrive on time

items.q: Oliver must be in Hobart city by 08:15. What is the latest bus he can catch from Kingston?
items.e: Look along the Hobart city row for the last time that is not after 08:15: 08:06. Go up that column to Kingston: 07:40. The next bus gets to Hobart city at 08:26, which is too late.

items.q: Mei must be at Sandy Bay by 07:50. What is the latest bus she can catch from Taroona?
items.e: In the Sandy Bay row, the last time not after 07:50 is 07:42. Go up that column to the Taroona row: 07:34. The 07:49 bus from Taroona reaches Sandy Bay at 07:57, which is too late.

items.q: Jack gets to the Kingston stop at 07:31. What time is the next bus?
items.e: The 07:25 bus has already gone. The next time in the Kingston row is 07:40. (07:34 is in the Taroona row.)

items.q: Amelia gets to the Taroona stop at 07:38. How long must she wait for the next bus?
items.e: The 07:34 bus has gone. The next bus from Taroona is at 07:49. 07:38 to 07:49 is 11 minutes. (07:40 is in the Kingston row, not the Taroona row.)

items.q: It takes Charlotte 15 minutes to walk to the Kingston stop. She wants to catch the 07:40 bus. What is the latest time she can leave home?
items.e: Work backwards: count back 15 minutes from 07:40. 07:40 − 15 minutes = 07:25. (Adding 15 minutes gives 07:55, after the bus has left.)

items.q: School in Sandy Bay starts at 08:40. It is a 6-minute walk from the Sandy Bay stop to school. What is the latest bus Lachlan can catch from Kingston?
items.e: He must be at the Sandy Bay stop by 08:40 − 6 minutes = 08:34. In the Sandy Bay row, the last time not after 08:34 is 08:17. Go up to Kingston: 08:00. (The 08:20 bus gets to Sandy Bay at 08:37, so he would be late after the walk.)

items.q: Sienna must be in Hobart city by 7:55 am. What is the latest bus she can catch from Sandy Bay?
items.e: 7:55 am is 07:55. In the Hobart city row, the last time not after 07:55 is 07:51. Go up to Sandy Bay: 07:42.

items.q: Ethan is at the Taroona stop at 07:52. What is the earliest time he can get to Hobart city?
items.e: The 07:49 bus from Taroona has gone. The next one is at 08:09. Go down that column to Hobart city: 08:26. (08:06 belongs to the bus that has already left.)

items.q: Leo catches the 07:40 bus from Kingston to Hobart city. His swimming lesson starts at 08:30. How long does he have between getting off the bus and the start of his lesson?
items.e: Go down the 07:40 column to Hobart city: 08:06. 08:06 to 08:30 is 24 minutes. (Starting from 07:40 gives 50 minutes, but that includes the bus ride.)

items.q: How many buses leave Kingston before 8 am?
items.e: 8 am is 08:00. In the Kingston row, 07:05, 07:25 and 07:40 are before 08:00, so 3 buses. The 08:00 bus leaves at 8 am, not before it.

items.q: A movie starts at 19:10. Kai wants to be there 10 minutes early. The bus trip takes 35 minutes. Buses leave at 18:05, 18:25 and 18:45. Which is the latest bus he can catch?
items.e: Work backwards: he must arrive by 19:10 − 10 minutes = 19:00. Then 19:00 − 35 minutes = 18:25. The latest bus at or before 18:25 is 18:25. (18:35 is not a bus time.)

items.q: Chloe’s family wants to watch the footy at the MCG, which starts at 19:40. The train takes 25 minutes, then they walk for 10 minutes. Trains leave at 18:52, 19:07 and 19:22. Which is the latest train that gets them there in time?
items.e: Work backwards: 19:40 − 10 minutes = 19:30, then 19:30 − 25 minutes = 19:05. The latest train not after 19:05 is 18:52. (The 19:07 train only works if you forget the walk.)

items.q: A netball game starts at 9:15 am. Players must arrive 20 minutes early. The drive takes 25 minutes. What is the latest time Matilda can leave home, in 24-hour time?
items.e: Count back 20 minutes from 09:15: 08:55. Then count back 25 minutes: 08:30. It is in the morning, so it is 08:30, not 20:30.

items.q: Aarav’s train gets to the interchange at 08:47. It takes him 5 minutes to walk to the bus stop. Buses leave at 08:40, 08:55 and 09:10. Which bus can he catch?
items.e: He can be at the bus stop at 08:47 + 5 minutes = 08:52. The 08:40 bus has gone, so the first bus he can catch is 08:55. (08:52 is not a bus time.)

items.q: Ferries from Circular Quay to Manly leave on the hour and at half past. The trip takes 30 minutes. Harper’s family gets to Circular Quay at 10:40. What time do they get to Manly?
items.e: The 10:30 ferry has gone. The next one leaves at 11:00. 11:00 + 30 minutes = 11:30. (11:10 forgets the wait for the ferry.)

items.q: Trains leave a station every 12 minutes, starting at 06:10. William gets to the station at 07:00. What time is the next train?
items.e: Count on in 12s: 06:10, 06:22, 06:34, 06:46, 06:58, 07:10. The 06:58 train has gone, so the next is 07:10. (Trains do not have to leave on the hour.)

items.q: Coaches from Adelaide to Victor Harbor leave at 08:30, 11:30 and 16:00. The trip takes 1 hour 35 minutes. Isla wants to be in Victor Harbor by 1:30 pm. Which is the latest coach she can catch?
items.e: 1:30 pm is 13:30. 13:30 − 1 hour 35 minutes = 11:55. The latest coach not after 11:55 is 11:30; it arrives at 13:05. (13:05 is the arrival time, not a coach time.)

items.q: Buses to the beach leave every 15 minutes from 08:50. The trip takes 48 minutes. Jack wants to be at the beach by 10:30 am. Which is the latest bus he can catch?
items.e: Work backwards: 10:30 − 48 minutes = 09:42. The buses are 08:50, 09:05, 09:20, 09:35, 09:50. The latest one not after 09:42 is 09:35 (it arrives at 10:23). The 09:50 bus arrives at 10:38, too late.

items.q: Grace can go to the zoo two ways. Train: leaves 08:05, arrives 08:52, then a 6-minute walk. Bus: leaves 08:12, arrives 09:04, then a 2-minute walk. Which way gets her to the zoo first, and by how much?
items.e: Find the time she reaches the zoo each way. Train: 08:52 + 6 minutes = 08:58. Bus: 09:04 + 2 minutes = 09:06. 08:58 to 09:06 is 8 minutes, so the train is 8 minutes earlier. (Comparing only the arrival times forgets the walks.)

items.q: Mia’s flight leaves at 14:20. She must be at the airport 1 hour before. The drive to the airport takes 50 minutes. What is the latest time she can leave home?
items.e: Work backwards: 14:20 − 1 hour = 13:20 (at the airport). Then 13:20 − 50 minutes = 12:30. (13:30 forgets the hour at the airport; 16:10 adds instead of counting back.)

sets.title: Itineraries: a school camp and a day trip

items.q: How long is the bus trip from school to camp?
items.e: Count on: 08:15 to 09:00 is 45 minutes, 09:00 to 11:00 is 2 hours, 11:00 to 11:40 is 40 minutes. 2 hours + 45 minutes + 40 minutes = 3 hours 25 minutes.

items.q: How long is canoeing?
items.e: Count on: 13:00 to 14:00 is 1 hour, 14:00 to 14:45 is 45 minutes. 1 hour + 45 minutes = 1 hour 45 minutes.

items.q: How long is free time?
items.e: Count on: 17:35 to 18:00 is 25 minutes. So it is 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: What are the students doing at 4:20 pm?
items.e: 4:20 pm is 16:20 (4 + 12 = 16). The bushwalk starts at 15:10 and free time starts at 17:35, so at 16:20 they are on the bushwalk. (Reading 4:20 pm as 14:20 gives canoeing.)

items.q: What are the students doing at 7:50 pm?
items.e: 7:50 pm is 19:50 (7 + 12 = 19). The night walk starts at 19:15 and lights out is at 20:45, so it is the night walk. (Reading 7:50 pm as 17:50 gives free time.)

items.q: How long is it from arriving at camp to the start of canoeing?
items.e: Count on: 11:40 to 12:00 is 20 minutes, 12:00 to 13:00 is 1 hour. 1 hour + 20 minutes = 1 hour 20 minutes. (Doing 1300 − 1140 = 160 and calling it 1 hour 60 minutes uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: How long is it from the start of dinner to lights out?
items.e: Count on: 18:00 to 20:00 is 2 hours, 20:00 to 20:45 is 45 minutes. 2 hours + 45 minutes = 2 hours 45 minutes.

items.q: How long is the bushwalk?
items.e: Count on: 15:10 to 16:00 is 50 minutes, 16:00 to 17:00 is 1 hour, 17:00 to 17:35 is 35 minutes. 1 hour + 50 minutes + 35 minutes = 2 hours 25 minutes.

items.q: On day 2 the students wake up at 06:45. How long is it from lights out to waking up?
items.e: Count on: 20:45 to 21:00 is 15 minutes, 21:00 to 06:00 is 9 hours, 06:00 to 06:45 is 45 minutes. 9 hours + 15 minutes + 45 minutes = 10 hours. (20:45 − 06:45 = 14 hours is the wrong way round, and stopping at midnight gives only 3 hours 15 minutes.)

items.q: Canoeing runs 20 minutes late, so afternoon tea starts 20 minutes late. Afternoon tea still lasts 25 minutes. What time does the bushwalk start now?
items.e: Afternoon tea starts at 14:45 + 20 minutes = 15:05. It lasts 25 minutes (14:45 to 15:10), so 15:05 + 25 minutes = 15:30.

items.q: How long is the drive from Melbourne to the koala reserve?
items.e: Count on: 09:30 to 10:00 is 30 minutes, 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour, 11:00 to 11:35 is 35 minutes. 1 hour + 30 minutes + 35 minutes = 2 hours 5 minutes.

items.q: How long does the family spend at the koala reserve?
items.e: Count on: 11:35 to 12:00 is 25 minutes, 12:00 to 13:00 is 1 hour. 1 hour + 25 minutes = 1 hour 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is the family away from home, from leaving Melbourne to arriving home?
items.e: Count on: 09:30 to 10:00 is 30 minutes, 10:00 to 21:00 is 11 hours, 21:00 to 21:10 is 10 minutes. 11 hours + 30 minutes + 10 minutes = 11 hours 40 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is the drive home?
items.e: Count on: 19:00 to 21:00 is 2 hours, 21:00 to 21:10 is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 10 minutes = 2 hours 10 minutes.

items.q: What is the family doing at 3 pm?
items.e: 3 pm is 15:00. The beach walk starts at 14:10 and the Nobbies boardwalk starts at 16:15, so they are on the beach walk. (Reading 3 pm as 13:00 gives lunch.)

items.q: What time does the Penguin Parade start, in 12-hour time?
items.e: 17 is more than 12, so it is pm. 17 − 12 = 5, so 17:30 is 5:30 pm. (Dropping the 1 gives 7:30 pm.)

items.q: The family leaves Melbourne 25 minutes late, and every part of the day moves 25 minutes later. What time do they get home?
items.e: Add 25 minutes to 21:10: 21:10 + 25 minutes = 21:35.

items.q: In July, Perth time is 2 hours behind Sydney time. Grandma calls from Perth at 18:30 Perth time. What time is it in Sydney?
items.e: Sydney is 2 hours ahead of Perth, so add 2 hours: 18:30 + 2 hours = 20:30. (Taking away 2 hours gives the wrong direction.)

items.q: In July, Perth is 2 hours behind Sydney. A flight leaves Sydney at 08:00 Sydney time and takes 5 hours 20 minutes. What time does it land, in Perth time?
items.e: 08:00 + 5 hours 20 minutes = 13:20 Sydney time. Perth is 2 hours behind, so 13:20 − 2 hours = 11:20 Perth time. (13:20 forgets the time difference.)

items.q: In July, Sydney is 2 hours ahead of Perth. A flight leaves Perth at 13:35 Perth time and takes 4 hours 15 minutes. What time does it land, in Sydney time?
items.e: 13:35 + 4 hours 15 minutes = 17:50 Perth time. Sydney is 2 hours ahead, so 17:50 + 2 hours = 19:50 Sydney time. (17:50 forgets the time difference.)

items.q: Aarav catches the 16:42 tram home. The tram ride takes 28 minutes, then he walks for 7 minutes. What time does he get home?
items.e: 16:42 + 28 minutes = 17:10 (18 minutes to 17:00, then 10 more). Then 17:10 + 7 minutes = 17:17.

items.q: A Year 6 excursion bus leaves school at 09:05. The trip to the museum takes 50 minutes. The class spends 2 hours 15 minutes in the museum and 30 minutes having lunch, then takes the 50-minute trip back. What time do they get back to school?
items.e: 09:05 + 50 minutes = 09:55. 09:55 + 2 hours 15 minutes = 12:10. 12:10 + 30 minutes = 12:40. 12:40 + 50 minutes = 13:30. Remember the trip back.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, 14 races are swum one after another, starting at 09:30. Each race takes 6 minutes. What time do the races finish?
items.e: 14 × 6 = 84 minutes = 1 hour 24 minutes. 09:30 + 1 hour 24 minutes = 10:54. (84 minutes is not 0 hours 84 minutes, so 10:14 is wrong.)

items.q: A netball game has 4 quarters of 10 minutes. There are breaks of 3 minutes, 5 minutes and 3 minutes between the quarters. The game starts at 08:40. What time does it finish?
items.e: Playing time: 4 × 10 = 40 minutes. Breaks: 3 + 5 + 3 = 11 minutes. 40 + 11 = 51 minutes. 08:40 + 51 minutes = 09:31. (There are only 3 breaks between 4 quarters.)

items.q: A day of cricket runs from 10:00 to 17:00, with a 40-minute lunch break and a 20-minute tea break. How much time is spent playing?
items.e: 10:00 to 17:00 is 7 hours. The breaks are 40 + 20 = 60 minutes = 1 hour. 7 hours − 1 hour = 6 hours.

items.q: It is 21:40 on 31 December. How long is it until the midnight fireworks?
items.e: Count on: 21:40 to 22:00 is 20 minutes, 22:00 to 00:00 is 2 hours. 2 hours + 20 minutes = 2 hours 20 minutes. (Midnight is 24:00 at the end of the day. Doing 2400 − 2140 = 260 uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: A nurse starts a night shift at 21:30 and works for 10 hours. What time does the shift end?
items.e: 21:30 + 2 hours 30 minutes = 24:00, which is midnight (00:00). 10 hours − 2 hours 30 minutes = 7 hours 30 minutes. 00:00 + 7 hours 30 minutes = 07:30 the next morning. (A 24-hour time never goes past 23:59.)

items.q: Cooper’s family catches a 09:48 train from Brisbane to the Gold Coast. The train takes 1 hour 15 minutes, then a bus to the theme park takes 20 minutes. What time do they get to the theme park?
A movie starts at 7:15 pm. Ruby’s family wants 1 hour for dinner before it, and it takes 25 minutes to drive to the restaurant. What is the latest time they can leave home, in 24-hour time?
items.e: 7:15 pm is 19:15. Count back 1 hour: 18:15. Count back 25 minutes: 15 minutes to 18:00, then 10 more: 17:50. It is the evening, so it is 17:50, not 05:50.

items.q: Zara’s family gets to a wildlife park at 13:55. The platypus tour starts at 14:20. How long do they wait?
items.e: Count on: 13:55 to 14:00 is 5 minutes, 14:00 to 14:20 is 20 minutes. 5 minutes + 20 minutes = 25 minutes. (1420 − 1355 = 65 uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: A school fun run starts at 7:45 am. Noah finishes at 9:12 am. How long does he take?
items.e: Count on: 7:45 am to 8:00 am is 15 minutes, 8:00 am to 9:00 am is 1 hour, 9:00 am to 9:12 am is 12 minutes. 1 hour + 15 minutes + 12 minutes = 1 hour 27 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Liam leaves home at 07:52. He walks to the bus stop in 8 minutes, waits 6 minutes, then rides the bus for 22 minutes. What time does he get to school?
items.e: 8 + 6 + 22 = 36 minutes. 07:52 + 36 minutes: 8 minutes to 08:00, then 28 more = 08:28. (Remember the waiting time.)

items.q: An overnight ferry across Bass Strait leaves at 19:30 and arrives at 06:30 the next morning. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 19:30 to 20:00 is 30 minutes, 20:00 to 06:00 is 10 hours, 06:00 to 06:30 is 30 minutes. 10 hours + 30 minutes + 30 minutes = 11 hours. (19:30 − 06:30 = 13 hours is the wrong way round.)

items.q: A Year 6 class plans a city day. They start at 09:20, spend 1 hour 15 minutes at the museum, walk for 30 minutes to the art gallery, then spend 45 minutes there. What time do they finish at the gallery?
items.e: 1 hour 15 minutes + 30 minutes + 45 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. 09:20 + 2 hours 30 minutes = 11:50.

items.q: Trains leave a station at 10, 30 and 50 minutes past every hour. Charlotte gets to the station at 08:07. How long must she wait?
items.e: The trains around then leave at 07:50, 08:10 and 08:30. At 08:07 the next train is at 08:10, so she waits 3 minutes.

items.q: A movie starts at 19:35 and is 1 hour 50 minutes long. Isla’s bedtime is 9:15 pm. When does the movie end?
items.e: 19:35 + 1 hour 50 minutes = 21:25. 9:15 pm is 21:15. 21:15 to 21:25 is 10 minutes, so it ends 10 minutes after her bedtime.

items.q: A family drives from Sydney to Canberra. The driving takes 3 hours 15 minutes and they stop for 25 minutes on the way. They leave at 08:50. What time do they get to Canberra?
items.e: 3 hours 15 minutes + 25 minutes = 3 hours 40 minutes. 08:50 + 3 hours = 11:50. 11:50 + 40 minutes = 12:30.

items.q: Sienna has swimming training from 06:15 to 07:30 on 4 mornings a week. How much training time is that each week?
items.e: 06:15 to 07:30 is 1 hour 15 minutes. 4 × 1 hour = 4 hours and 4 × 15 minutes = 60 minutes = 1 hour. 4 hours + 1 hour = 5 hours.

items.q: The camp bus leaves at 07:45. The driving takes 3 hours 50 minutes, plus a 20-minute stop. Lunch at camp is at 12:30. How long is it from arriving at camp to lunch?
items.e: 3 hours 50 minutes + 20 minutes = 4 hours 10 minutes. 07:45 + 4 hours 10 minutes = 11:55. Count on: 11:55 to 12:00 is 5 minutes, 12:00 to 12:30 is 30 minutes. 5 minutes + 30 minutes = 35 minutes.

items.q: In July, Perth is 2 hours behind Sydney. A flight leaves Sydney at 17:30 Sydney time and lands in Perth at 20:50 Perth time. How long is the flight?
items.e: Change the landing time to Sydney time: 20:50 + 2 hours = 22:50. Count on: 17:30 to 18:00 is 30 minutes, 18:00 to 22:00 is 4 hours, 22:00 to 22:50 is 50 minutes. 4 hours + 30 minutes + 50 minutes = 5 hours 20 minutes. (3 hours 20 minutes forgets the time difference.)
